preamble: Place assimilation and fortition of the coda tap [ɾ] to the voiced bilabial stop [b] before a labial stop. In western Cuban Spanish, coda /ɾ/ and coda /l/ merge and assimilate to the next consonant; before /b/ and /p/ they surface as an unreleased [b˺], a geminate in curva cu[b˺b]a and a voiced-voiceless sequence in cuerpo cue[b˺p]o. The unassimilated pronunciations remain more common. Before /p/ the descriptions differ: Guitart (1978, 2004) describes the first element as non-occlusive [β˺p], and Lamb (1968) and Ruiz Hernández (1974) report a voiceless [pp], while a later acoustic study by Ruiz Hernández and Miyares Bermúdez (1984) found the first element voiced in all examples (all as summarized by Arias 2019).
phoneticEffects: Regressive Assimilation, Place Assimilation, Fortition, Gemination

examples.note: [b˺] is an unreleased voiced bilabial stop.
Homophonous with silba 'he/she whistles', because coda /l/ assimilates in the same way.
Before voiceless /p/ the assimilated tap stays voiced; culpa gives cu[b˺p]a from coda /l/.

sources: Arias Cabal, Á. (2019). Fonética y fonología de las consonantes geminadas en el español de Cuba. Moenia, 25, 465–497. https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/moenia/article/view/6474
